summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, diastolic heart failure, polymyositis, and chronic anticoagulation for recurrent DVT/PE was admitted with right upper thigh pain and fever. She was found to have a cutaneous abscess that was initially drained in the emergency department. Due to persistent pain and imaging confirmation of a residual fluid collection, she underwent a second ultrasound-guided drainage. Cultures from the abscess grew Proteus mirabilis, and her antibiotics were narrowed from intravenous vancomycin and Zosyn to oral ciprofloxacin. Her warfarin was continued throughout with a therapeutic INR at discharge, though she was counseled on potential interaction with ciprofloxacin requiring close INR monitoring at home. Her other chronic conditions remained stable. She improved clinically, completed necessary procedures, and was discharged home with a plan to finish a 7-day course of antibiotics, follow up with her primary care provider, and monitor her INR.
problems: Body mass index [BMI] 70 or greater, adult
Proteus (mirabilis) (morganii) as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
